messages:
anya-support: FYI — Acme reported a sustained increase in 503s + client-side timeouts hitting our hosted /v1/generate endpoint since ~10:45 PDT. Their SDK is retrying aggressively and they're seeing billing anomalies. Pasting the customer's minimal repro & logs they shared below. @sam-sre can you triage?

anya-support: Customer notes: us-west region, ~120 concurrent open requests for a short window, streaming enabled, each request ~8k tokens prompt + generation. They see 503 followed by SDK retry loop (exponential backoff exhausted).

anya-support: Customer-provided log snippet:
```
req_id=rc-9f7a2b status=503 backend=gw-edge-03 latency_ms=30245 route=/v1/generate client_retry=3
error="upstream response: service unavailable"
sdk_log: "Request failed, retrying in 500ms (attempt 2)"
```

sam-sre: Thanks. Quick Qs: exact curl or SDK call + headers? any auth failures (401/403) or strictly 5xx?

anya-support: No auth errors. Here's the curl they ran (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","stream":true,"input":"<~8k token prompt>"}' \
```

deploy-bot: deploy completed: edge-proxy v2.14 -> ca-central (2026-03-12T09:40:00Z) :rocket:

connie-eng: Hypothesis: edge L7 proxy is returning 503 after ~30s when request processing gets queued due to KV cache lock contention + CPU saturation on a subset of serving nodes. If SDK keeps streaming connections open and we hit connection limits, proxies start rejecting.

connie-eng: Can we repro with their exact concurrency? Steps I'd use: 1) Spawn 60-120 concurrent streaming requests from us-west. 2) Each with ~8k token prompts and streaming enabled. 3) Observe edge->runtime spans & per-tenant queue lengths.

sam-sre: Mitigations to try while we investigate:
- Ask customer to reduce concurrency to ~20 for a short window.
- Add a temporary rate-limiter rule for this tenant at the edge (soft 50rps burst).
- Route their traffic to model variant with lower memory/compute (quantized) to reduce CPU pressure.

anya-support: I'll propose those to Acme now. Also adding repro steps I can run from our side.

anya-support: Local repro script (node/python pseudo) I'm going to run:
```python
# high-level: spawn N concurrent SDK streaming calls
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=...)
async def worker(i):
    await client.generate_stream(model="redwood-large", input=big_prompt)
# spawn 80 workers at once and observe status codes / errors\```

anya-support: First run: reproduced 503s within ~2 minutes. Dump from our edge logs: 
```
[edge] ts=2026-03-12T17:12:05 req=rc-9f7a2b status=503 node=gw-edge-07 queued_ms=31240 backend_try=1
[rt] ts=2026-03-12T17:12:05 req=rc-9f7a2b err="kvcache_lock_timeout"
```

sam-sre: Good repro. Looking at runtime metrics now — a subset of serving hosts show queue depth spike and 95th latency > 28s, CPU usage > 85% on impacted nodes. Not seeing OOMs. Likely contention on KV cache locks + request scheduling causing tail latency and proxy 503s.

connie-eng: Action plan:
- Short-term (hours): apply per-tenant rate limit at edge + route customer to a lower-cost model variant. I can push a conservative edge rule (50rps) as a config change.
- Medium-term (days): increase KV cache lock timeout, add backpressure signals to scheduler, and tune batching thresholds for long-context streaming workloads.
- Communicate: support will offer Dedicated option for sustained high-concurrency large-context workloads.

connie-eng: I'll open PR to edge-config -> refs: PR#4561 and will coordinate a 1h rollout window.

sam-sre: I'll prepare a temporary routing rule and a mitigation playbook snippet we can paste to the customer.

anya-support: Customer update (outbound): "Thanks — we've reproduced the issue and are applying a temporary rate limit and routing change to reduce errors. Short-term workaround: reduce your concurrency to 20 or request Dedicated capacity. We expect fewer 503s within 15-30 minutes after config is applied. We'll follow up with post-mortem and permanent fixes"

anya-support: Posting follow-up when edge rule + route completed.

deploy-bot: edge-config PR#4561 merged by connie-eng; rollout started 2026-03-12T17:34:00Z

anya-support: Mitigation applied and customer notified. They reported immediate drop in 503s but latency still slightly elevated p95. Customer accepted temporary cadence and asked for a note when medium-term fixes are planned.

sam-sre: Adding this to the incidents backlog (INC-2026-03) for tracking medium-term work and eval on quotas.

connie-eng: I'll schedule follow-up demo with SRE & Product to discuss Dedicated offer for Acme and tuning KV cache parameters.

anya-support: Thanks team — closing this Slack thread once we have the post-mortem and timeline. :white_check_mark:
